subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should cron `every` gain a deterministic phase/stagger/prime contract, and what public schema, CLI flags, defaults, and upgrade behavior should own it?
rationale: The missing behavior is real in source, but adding it changes public scheduling semantics and persisted cron job shape, so automation should not choose the product contract or defaults alone.

options.title: Add Opt-In Every Phase
options.body: Preserve current exact `every` behavior by default, add one explicit phase/stagger option with persistence, CLI/docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Make Every Phase Default
options.body: Spread load automatically for every jobs, but accept an upgrade-visible schedule timing change that needs stronger migration and release communication.

options.title: Document Existing Paths Only
options.body: Leave cron `every` exact, keep top-of-hour stagger on cron expressions, and document heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger as the supported anti-herd paths.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Every Phase
recommendation.body: Preserve current exact `every` behavior by default, add one explicit phase/stagger option with persistence, CLI/docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the existing cron stagger controls and are the best available routing owner for the cron scheduling contract choice.
